column1: # X11 P1 — POPULATION of the final-vocabulary decision table.
# This file carries no decision. It is the mechanical half of
# `01-decision-table.md`: every published name, in every role it plays, with
# the properties a decision leans on. There is deliberately no `decision`,
# `proposed` or `reason` column — those are P1's own step, made against this
# THE UNIT OF A ROW IS A NAME IN A ROLE, NOT A NAME. `complexity.cyclomatic`
# is a channel code, a producer rule name AND a metric key; each is a separate
# row with the same `name` and a different `role`, because one row could not
# express "rename the channel, keep the key". 118 of the 314 rows share their
# spelling with at least one other row; `coincides_with` names the other roles.
# ROW COUNT: 314 = 58 channel codes + 82 metric keys + 51 producer rule names
# + 43 rule option keys + 80 CLI flag aliases. `set` and `role` are in 1:1
# correspondence by construction (the set is the population, the role is what
# a name does in it); both columns are kept because `01-decision-table.md`
# STEP 1 — the five oracles, from the PRODUCTION container. Write the script
# below to `oracles.php` at the repository root and run it. It boots the real
# container, resolves a configuration document the way `check` does, and
# dumps every oracle to `raw.json`. The working directory it resolves the
# document in is an EMPTY directory (`mktemp -d`) with no `qmx.yaml` in it or
# above it: this repository's own `qmx.yaml` could exclude health dimensions,
# and the run must see the shipped defaults instead.
# `raw.json` lands beside this file because the SELF-CHECK block below runs
# from THIS directory (it also reads ../enumeration-renames.tsv). It is a
# scratch product of the measurement, not a tracked artifact: delete it once
#   channels=58 rules=51 metrics=82 aliases=80 optionKeys=43 checkOptions=80
# // A throwaway command carrying the real check definition, so ArrayInput binds
# // and `addOptions()` reports the dynamically registered rule flags.
# // Without this the computed-metric catalog is empty and `channels()` answers
# // the 52 static codes only — the run-time `health.*` family exists only once
# // a configuration document has been resolved.
# // constructor parameter names + declared shorthand keys + declared
# // additional keys, plus the three framework keys it hard-codes.
# fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("channels=%d rules=%d metrics=%d aliases=%d optionKeys=%d checkOptions=%d\n",
#     count($channels), count($rules), count($metrics), count($aliases), count($optionKeys), count($checkOptionNames)));
# The oracle for channel codes is `ChannelIdentityInterface::channels()` and
# NOT `staticDeclarations()`, which excludes the run-time family by
# construction (its own docblock says so). The 58 are the 52 static codes plus
# STEP 2 — the derived columns, joined onto three existing artifacts of this
# `set`    — which of the five oracle sets it came from.
# `role`   — what the name does: channel-code | metric-key |
#                        verbatim for the 52 static codes. The six `health.*`
#                        codes have no row there; they were classified by that
#                        file's own published rule (applied to the SECOND
#                        each a measurable dimension, so all six are `subject`.
#   producer-rule-name — THE SAME channel rule, because 43 of the 51 producer
#                        names have a row in enumeration-channel-naming.tsv and
#                        are copied from it. The eight that do NOT have one:
#                        the six `health.*` names — which are channel codes in
#                        this file too, but run-time ones, absent from that
#                        deliberate widening of that rule's clause 2, named
#                        here because it is the only row it applies to: the
#                        segment `directive` names the ENTITY the rule
#                        examines rather than a measurable dimension, and it
#                        is plainly neither a verdict (clause 3) nor a PHP
#                        second dot-segment at all — the only single-segment
#                        name in any of the five sets — so it is
#                        `no-second-segment`, a sixth value this file adds and
#   rule-option-key    — a five-way rule on the canonical (kebab-folded) key:
#                        `level` — the key is spelled exactly like a
#                          `namespace`), i.e. it introduces a nested per-level
#                          option map rather than carrying a value;
#                        `word` — a single word that is none of the above
#   cli-flag-alias     — a three-way rule on the alias against the option name
#                          i.e. it ends in `-warning`, `-error`, or in the
#                          kebab spelling of the option's last dot-segment,
#                        `option-only` — the alias IS the kebab spelling of
#                          that leaf, with no rule designator
#                        `rule-only` — the alias carries no option designator
# `declared_as` — the raw spelling(s) the code declares, when they differ from
#   the canonical `name`. Only rule option keys have any: their declarations
#   are a mixture of camelCase constructor parameters, snake_case
#   `ConfigKeySpelling::normalize()` folds all three into one key. The
#   canonical spelling published here is kebab-case, which is what
#   docblock name as the form a user writes in `qmx.yaml`, presets and
#   `--rule-opt`. The fold merged no two distinct declarations: 43 raw
#   role has, filled per role and empty where there is none:
#     channel-code       owner = the producing rule name
#                        for the six `health.*` codes, itself — a built-in
#                        dimension is its own producer, per
#     metric-key         owner = the key's family (first dot-segment).
#     producer-rule-name owner = the name's first dot-segment;
#                        addresses = the channel codes it produces.
#     rule-option-key    owner = the rule that declares it, or `<shared>`;
#                        owner_count = how many rules declare it;
#                        addresses = all of them, when more than one.
#     cli-flag-alias     owner = the rule the CliAlias attribute sits on;
#                        addresses = the option name it sets, verbatim
# `sites` — the sum of the eight per-surface occurrence columns
#   Those columns count occurrences of the string LITERAL, so they cannot
#   distinguish a name's roles. That is also where the six `health.*` CHANNEL
#   rows get their count: from their `producer` row, the only row those names
#   have there. All 43 names that have both a `channel` and a
#   `producer` row there carry identical counts in both, verified by
#   comparison (see SELF-CHECK). Empty — never `0` — for a name that artifact
#   does not carry at all: 123 rows, being every rule option key (43) and
#   every CLI alias (80). No name is missing for any other reason.
# `frozen` — `kind` / `leaf` / `no`, derived from the four DERIVED columns of
#   ../enumeration-renames.tsv and never from a hand list:
#   -> `leaf`; else `no`. Read from the row of the MATCHING kind, so this
#   column is role-specific where `sites` is not. Channel rows: 6 `kind`,
#   12 `leaf`, 34 `no`. Every `metric-key` and `producer` row of that artifact
#   has zero in all four columns, so all 82 metric-key and 51
#   producer-rule-name rows here are `no`. Empty for the 129 rows with no row
#   of their kind in that artifact: the 123 above plus the six `health.*`
#   CHANNEL rows (which are present there as producers, not as channels).
#   NOTE: `01-decision-table.md` writes this column's values as
#   `kind`/`bag`/`no`; the second value is spelled `leaf` here, after the
#   `leaf_const`/`leaf_pin` columns it is actually derived from.
# `migration_class` — what happens to a CONSUMER who does not follow a rename
#   of this name, chosen per ROLE from enumeration-migration-surfaces.tsv.
#   One name reaches several surfaces with different loudness, so the single
#   value published is the QUIETEST class among the surfaces that role
#   appears on, ordered silent < warn-and-default < inert-detected <
#   nothing is lost by the fold. `shipped_migration` is a separate axis — not
#   "how loud is the failure" but "does a shipped command carry the old data
#   across" — and is `yes` only for channel codes, which
#   All five classes were MEASURED on a throwaway tree outside the repository
#   (one class, seven-boolean-parameter file; no `composer.json`), with a
#                      -> "Carried 7 of 9 entries onto a new channel name.",
#                         exit 0; the "channel" field is rewritten in place.
#                      An unknown CLI FLAG is refused by Symfony instead:
#                      -> '"--max-nonexistent" option does not exist.' and the
#                         usage line, EXIT 1, not 3. Same class, different
#                         exit code; the code is recorded here rather than
#                         no channel. ...', exit 2. The rename is DETECTED, but
#                         as a finding in the consumer's own report, not as a
#                         callable, class, threshold' on stderr, the run
#                         continues with the default, exit 2 (from the
#                         findings, not from the option). The same key given as
#                         produces the identical warning and continues.
#                      Both publish the name into an artifact a consumer
#                      stores and matches on, and NEITHER has any product-side
#                      reader: the four classes above are the complete list of
#                      detections this product performs, and no detection
#                      `check_name` or a dashboard's metric-key column. That
#                      absence is what `silent` names, and it is why
#                      channel-code and metric-key rows fold to `silent`.
# `coincides_with` — the other roles carried by the identical spelling,
#   comma-separated; empty when the name is unique to its role.
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE
#     configuration; the run above used an empty working directory, so it
#     reports the six built-in `health.*` dimensions and no `computed.*` name.
#     That half of the vocabulary is open by construction — its names come out
#     of a consumer's own `qmx.yaml` — and can only be observed, never
#     (`computed.branch-load`, from the finding-gate corpus). The producer
#     rule name `computed` IS in this file; the channels it produces are not,
#     and its `addresses` column is empty for that reason.
#  2. NESTED RULE OPTION KEYS. The oracle reproduces
#     keys only. Keys inside a per-level map — the `warning`/`error` under
#     `CliAlias` attributes address as `class.max_warning` — are not rows
#     here. `max_warning` and `max_error` therefore appear in this file only
#     inside the `addresses` column of the aliases that set them.
#     enumerable published strings that are NOT names in any of the five sets.
#     enumeration-migration-surfaces.tsv records the last of these as a
#     distinct role; none of them is populated here.
#  4. THE STATIC `check` OPTIONS. The ~40 hand-written flags of
#     `--workers`, …) are not in the `cli-flag-aliases` set: that set is
#     returns exactly those 80 as its dynamic list, and they are exactly the
#     alias keys.) A rename of `--format` is a real vocabulary change this
#  5. `sites` CANNOT SEPARATE ROLES, so summing the column over the whole file
#     double-counts every one of the 43 names that is both a channel code and
#     a producer rule name, and every one that is also a metric key. Use the
#     per-role rows, never the column total.
#  6. `sites` IS ALSO NOT A RENAME COST. It counts occurrences of a literal
#     across eight surfaces of THIS repository; a consumer's configuration,
#     directives, dashboards and stored suppressions are outside every one of
#     those surfaces, and the `silent` rows are exactly where that matters
#  7. `current_form` IS A READING, NOT A MEASUREMENT — for all five sets. Two
#     of them inherit that caveat verbatim from the files they copy (see the
#     `ambiguous` rows of enumeration-channel-naming.tsv); the three new rules
#     above are mechanical on the string, but the CHOICE of categories is
#  8. NO RULE-NAME-ONLY PUBLICATION SURFACE WAS FOUND, which is why
#     That is an absence measured against enumeration-migration-surfaces.tsv's
#     17 rows, not a proof: a report format that published a bare rule name
#     without a channel would be a silent surface this file misses.
#  9. THE JOIN IS BY SPELLING. `coincides_with` says two roles are spelled the
#     same, never that they mean the same thing; and a name absent from
#     ../enumeration-renames.tsv gets an empty `sites`, never a claim that it
# (b) `name`+`role` in this file == the union of the five oracles. The right
#     side is rebuilt from raw.json, so it re-runs the oracles rather than
# (d) `sites` is role-blind, as claimed above — the 43 names with both a
